ECB speeches and one-year OIS

When a policymaker signals tightening, does the market raise its expected rate path? Compare what ECB presidents and Executive Board members said with the change in euro overnight index swap rates during their speaking windows. The source includes parliamentary testimony as well as addresses.

3,868 communication windows · 2,475 matched full texts · 97 scored speeches · 14 speakers with a score

Cross-asset speech windowsMarket resultsPresidents and economic cyclesRead the speechesMethod and data

How often did the two agree?

48 scored speeches had a one-year OIS quote in regular trading hours on a non-meeting day with no overlapping ECB speaker window. Of these, 41 signalled directional policy guidance. One-year OIS moved by at most 1 bp in 34. Among the remaining 7, the sign of the OIS move agreed with the text in 5 and pointed the other way in 2.

Method and data

Coverage runs from 2000-01-08 to 2026-06-30. Dates, single-speaker names and full titles must match uniquely across the two ECB datasets after normalising case, punctuation and diacritics. The download includes every full-text match. A blank score means the record has no assigned reading. We selected and reviewed explicit policy passages before comparing their market moves. Selection favours recognisable English rate guidance, particularly the years of repeated low-rate commitments. The sample cannot establish which president was most hawkish.

+2 signals explicit tightening, +1 conditional tightening, 0 endorsement of the current setting, −1 conditional easing and −2 explicit easing or a commitment to prolonged accommodation. Hypothetical examples, past decisions and tools without a rate direction do not by themselves earn a score. Earlier scores are ordinal. They cannot be converted into basis points.

The ECB workbook compares median quotes 20–10 minutes before a speech begins with quotes 10–20 minutes after an assumed 30-minute speech ends. Positive OIS moves indicate higher market pricing at that tenor relative to the prespeech quote. One-year OIS reflects expected overnight rates over a year and a risk premium. The workbook publishes the change, so the level priced before a speech and individual-meeting probabilities remain unavailable from this source. German 2s10s is the ten-year yield minus the two-year yield. Unscheduled news can also move rates in the interval.
